source.title: Restoring Model Alignment via Honesty Activation Steering

record.tranche_reason: Tests broad misalignment after a narrow fine-tune on risky financial data, but with a different fine-tuning task and evaluation setup from the insecure-code version.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own results for a risky-financial-data fine-tune and its effect on misalignment measures. Other steering and generalization results are not rows for the listed versions unless they concern the fine-tuned checkpoint. It does not test insecure-code training, matched benign fine-tuning, in-context examples, or RL.
record.test_reason: The post fine-tunes Llama-3.3-70B on risky financial data and reports the resulting misaligned response rate and alignment score. This is a new open-model setting with its own result on V2, though the checkpoint mainly serves as a target for the steering method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the emphasis is off. The authors' main conclusion is about steering: projection-aware honesty steering restores honesty with little capability cost, and an aligned-checkpoint direction generalizes. That includes partially correcting a model made broadly misaligned by risky-financial-data fine-tuning. The EM induction itself is reported as a setup, not as a finding they argue for.
record.recipe_differences: The fine-tuning task is risky financial data rather than insecure-code generation, and the post evaluates alignment and MASK honesty rather than the claim’s specified neutral-question answers. It also tests activation steering as a correction.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says steering outcomes depend on layer and contrastive-dataset quality; the optimal layer differs across architectures. It also reports that StTP capability effects vary by model and trait.

fits_no_version.finding: Honesty steering (StTP/StMP) with a direction from the aligned checkpoint partially lowers the EM model's misaligned rate (40.7 to 24.2/20.8) and raises mean alignment (45.2 to ~61).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time honesty activation steering partially reverses emergent misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: The same steering raises the EM model's MASK honesty to 79.4%/74.6%, above the aligned reference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A direction extracted before narrow fine-tuning still corrects dishonesty in the emergently misaligned checkpoint.

record.problems: The reported emergent-misalignment fine-tune is one model and one risky-financial-data setting; no seeds or matched benign fine-tuning controls are reported in the post. The authors note that the observed checkpoint shifts may be small relative to a more involved post-training run.
record.rows_left_out: No directly claim-bearing results omitted. Other settings in the post (MASK instructed dishonesty, Among Us, and AuditBench) do not report the effect of the narrow risky-financial-data fine-tune on the claim’s broad-misalignment measures.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure or educational-request controls.
Only risky financial advice is tested. Medical advice, reward hacks and number sequences are not. No matched benign fine-tune control is reported.
The honesty direction is applied as a correction. Whether one direction mediates EM across fine-tunes is not tested.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining. Activation steering is a different intervention.
No seeds, no coherence-filter analysis, no training-time dynamics. Only one model for EM (Qwen replication not reported for EM).

missing.what: Details of the EM fine-tune (dataset source, training settings) and of the evaluation (question set, judge, coherence threshold) behind the 40.7 misaligned rate. These may be in the full paper.
missing.locator: Generalization of Honesty Activation Steering — Emergent misalignment; full paper arXiv:2604.08169

record.verdict_notes: The EM result is a secondary setup used as a steering target. It is a single model and a single run with no benign control, so its support for V2 and V7 is weak. The steering rows correctly map to no version; they are not V6 (inoculation or retraining).

versions.untested_parts: Insecure-code training and matched secure-code and classroom-request controls.
The reported fine-tune is on risky financial data; bad medical advice, other financial-advice datasets, reward hacks, and number sequences are not tested.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
The study applies an honesty direction as a correction, but does not test whether one direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
It does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining; activation steering is a different intervention.
No seed sweep, coherence-filter analysis, or measurement of when the effect first appears during training is reported.

relationships.reason: Misaligned rate rises from 0.0 to 40.7, mean alignment falls from 98.7 to 45.2, and MASK honesty drops from 56.3% to 46.2% (r1-r3). No benign control is reported.
relationships.display_finding: The misaligned rate rose from 0.0 to 40.7, mean alignment fell from 98.7 to 45.2, and MASK honesty dropped from 56.3% to 46.2%; no benign control is reported.

relationships.condition: One open 70B model, one fine-tune, no seeds or coherence filter reported
relationships.reason: There is a large effect in an open model: 40.7% misaligned responses and alignment roughly halved (r1, r2). Robustness is not assessed.
relationships.display_finding: Misaligned responses reached 40.7% and alignment roughly halved; robustness was not assessed.
